positive_control.expected: TP=1.0 on training split for drift patterns

null_control.expected: FP=0.0 on training split for fresh copies

observations: Fisher LDA ensemble of (1-Jaccard) and KS D on training split yields weights w=[-7.14, -1.33] with intercept 1.14, indicating both features inversely predict drift (higher divergence and KS D associated with noise, not drift)
Ensemble ROC on test split has AUC=0.625, only slightly above random (0.5)
No operating point on test ROC satisfies TP>=0.8 and FP<=0.15 simultaneously
Jaccard alone achieves TP=0.25, FP=0.25 at best Youden index on test set
KS D alone achieves TP=0.75, FP=0.50 at best Youden index on test set
Majority vote ensemble (both signals >0.5) yields TP=0.0, FP=0.25
Positive control fails: ensemble correctly classifies 0% of drift patterns on training set
Null control passes: ensemble correctly classifies 0% of fresh copies as drift on training set

The overlap between drift and noise conditions in the 2D feature space is substantial: noise patterns (optional_field_churn, null_valued_fields, nested_object_variation) have similar or higher Jaccard divergence and KS D than drift patterns
nested_object_variation (noise) has higher KS D (0.50-0.53) than most drift patterns, making it indistinguishable from drift in the temporal signal
validity_notes: Raw data from EXP-GRAPH-34788722106 (Jaccard) and EXP-GRAPH-35083040517 (response-time) are aggregated per-condition metrics (mean Jaccard, KS D), not per-sample. ROC is computed over 24 conditions (4 sizes x 6 patterns), not over individual samples. This is a severe limitation: the effective sample size is tiny, and variance estimates are unavailable.
The train/test split is 16/8 conditions, stratified by label. With only 8 test conditions, the ROC curve is coarse and operating points are limited.
The mock server produces computation-dependent timing (R^2=0.9999, +9.3ms/field), so temporal signals are confounded with structural complexity.
Fresh copies have Jaccard=1.0 and KS D ~0.13-0.27, making them easily distinguishable from drift and noise. However, fresh copies are not included in the primary discrimination task (drift vs noise).
The ensemble uses a linear discriminant, which may be insufficient for nonlinear decision boundaries. However, the spec mandates a linear discriminant.
Deterministic seed for train/test split (seed=20260916) ensures reproducibility.
unresolved: Whether a nonlinear ensemble (e.g., SVM, random forest) could achieve TP>=0.8 and FP<=0.15 given the feature overlap
Whether per-sample data (instead of aggregated per-condition metrics) would reveal different discrimination patterns
Whether additional features (e.g., KS p-value, Jaccard detection margin, schema size) could improve ensemble performance
Whether the inverted direction (noise more detectable than drift) is a fundamental property of the feature space or an artifact of the mock server design
Whether a different train/test split (e.g., leave-one-size-out) would yield different results
